## Problem
All four Codex profiles (codex, codex2, codex3, codex4) show "quota unavailable" for long periods although `codex` works from the CLI. Evidence I gathered:
- Daemon log ~/.local/share/mjolnir/logs/mj-daemon-20261106T114945.619Z-2087559.log: every ~10-30 minutes all four profiles fail together with "codex quota query failed: Codex app-server protocol error (Closed)", then succeed after the restart, then fail again. Earlier logs show the same pattern since at least 2026-11-05 17:18Z.
- The checks run in Podman containers (`mj-quota-*`, labels dev.mj.quota=true, dev.mj.instance=ee30cecc7a8152aa) started by the daemon's `mj node` process (pid 2087561).
- `podman events` shows the four containers created at 12:30:03Z were ended at 12:46:04-05Z with `stop` events on two and `died` on all four. The ones created 12:59:55Z ended the same way at 13:04:58-13:05:01Z. The probe found the stream Closed at the next poll (12:49:55, 13:09:54). So something outside the check removed live containers.
- Suspect (likely, NOT confirmed): `sweep_quota_containers` (mj-controller/src/quota_runtime.rs:355) runs `rm --force` on every quota container with this instance's label. It runs when any quota poller starts (`spawn_quota_refresher`, mj-controller/src/pollers/quota.rs:52-60). Instance identity is a hash of the data dir (`instance_identity_for`, mj-core/src/config/loading.rs:307), so any other process sharing the data dir that starts a quota poller (a second daemon/node, a TUI, a CLI command, a test run using the real data dir, `republish_quota_profiles` in mj-controller/src/server_runtime/actions.rs, etc.) would remove the live daemon's containers. Other possibilities to keep open: the daemon itself dropping/re-creating a `QuotaContainer` whose drop removes a container by the wrong name; a profile-batch restart; a different cleanup path (container GC, `mj recover`, orphan sweeps for dev.mj.managed=true) removing quota containers. Note many old `mj node` processes from Nov 4-5 with other instance labels are still alive and also have quota containers; a stray `mj node` or similar sharing ee30cecc might be the stopper.

## Assignment
1. Diagnose: identify which process/code path issues the stops at 12:46:04Z and 13:04:58Z (2026-11-06). Use `podman events --since ... --until ...` (add `--filter label=dev.mj.instance=ee30cecc7a8152aa`), daemon logs in ~/.local/share/mjolnir/logs (mj-daemon-*, mj-cli-*, mj-tui-* around those times), and the code. Read-only on the live system: do not stop, kill, or remove any process or container, and do not restart the daemon. Report confirmed vs likely.
2. Fix (decided direction): a cleanup must only remove quota containers whose owning process is dead, never ones a live process is using. Suggested approach: label each quota container with its owner (e.g. pid plus process start time or boot id, so pid reuse cannot fool it) and have the sweep skip containers whose owner is still alive; pick the exact shape yourself. If the diagnosis shows a different code path is the stopper, fix that path to the same rule. Keep the sweep's purpose (removing leftovers of a daemon that died mid-check). Do not add runtime self-audits; prove the rule with tests.
3. Validation: unit tests for the sweep decision (live owner kept, dead owner removed, unlabeled legacy containers handled sensibly — explain your choice). Run `cargo test -p mj-controller quota` in the foreground; clippy + fmt on changed code. Use cargo normally (mbx caching; do not redirect target/).

Status: sweep change is in; now adding the sweep-decision tests.

I've handed back my report. The fix is committed as `0d441003e` on `quota-sweep-owner` and not pushed.

The sweep now removes a quota container only when the process that started it has exited. I think the container stops come from test runs sharing the daemon's instance identity, but I haven't confirmed that.

- **Evidence:** Containers were removed at 12:46Z, 13:04Z and 13:21Z. The 13:21Z removals came 8 seconds before a `cargo test -p mj-controller` binary started on this host. Those tests start a quota poller, which runs the sweep. The daemon itself didn't restart in that window. I couldn't find what ran at 12:46 or 13:04, and I didn't run the old code against the live containers.
- **Fix:** Each quota container now carries an owner label (process id plus its birth identity, so a reused process id doesn't pass as the owner). The change is in `mj-controller/src/quota_runtime.rs` only, and `resolve` is untouched.
- **Old containers:** Containers with no owner label are kept, because the live daemon's current ones predate this build. They can live for days, so an age cutoff would be unsafe. Leftovers from older builds need a one-time manual `podman rm`.
- **Tests:** The six new unit tests pass. `cargo test -p brokk-mj-controller quota` gave 78 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored, and clippy and fmt are clean. No live quota containers were removed during that run.
- **Still open:** The live daemon runs the old build, so its containers stay exposed until it's reinstalled.
